ex5v9y:220: Traditional LLM applications follow a direct "input-output" mapping paradigm, where users expect the LLM to give the correct answer in one shot. AlphaEvolve, by contrast, embeds the LLM into an evolutionary loop of "generate-evaluate-retain-recombine," where the LLM's role is to continuously produce code mutations as a "mutation source." The deeper implication of this design is that the LLM does not need to generate the correct answer every time; it only needs to produce mutations that are better than existing solutions—the evolutionary system amplifies good mutations step by step through evaluation and selection. This means the boundary of AI capability expands from "how strong the model itself is" to "how well the evolutionary loop can amplify model capability."
